why_next: Within-stratum conditional permutation (the hypothesized fix for inherited C4 failure) FAILS to center null at zero: null_mean=0.417 bits (4.17x above 0.1 threshold). The bias floor ~0.41 bits is intrinsic to PMI estimator weighting across deterministic/stochastic strata (31.5% deterministic strata with PMI=0 dilute weighted average), not a permutation artifact. Convergence with action-shuffle (0.406 bits) confirms estimator-weighting property. The 0.933-bit K2 PMI signal remains reproducible but cannot support confirmatory beyond-Markov claim without valid null control. Alternative falsification frameworks are required: (a) model-based parametric bootstrap from estimated P(url_after|stratum) may eliminate finite-sample PMI log-ratio bias; (b) Miller-Madow unbiased PMI estimator may correct for small-stratum bias; (c) conditional entropy H(url_after|action,url_before,history) bypasses PMI weighting entirely. These are materially orthogonal to permutation-based methods and address the root cause (estimator bias, not permutation scheme).

recommended_action: Design a follow-up experiment with THREE materially orthogonal null frameworks to test whether alternative methods center null at zero for hash-routed SPAs: (1) Model-based parametric bootstrap: estimate P(url_after|url_before,history) from data, simulate null samples, compute PMI distribution. (2) Miller-Madow unbiased PMI estimator: apply bias correction to log-ratio estimator. (3) Conditional entropy H(url_after|action,url_before,history) as alternative to PMI, bypassing PMI weighting entirely. Test on same 12-state SPA with N=5000. If any framework centers null (|mean| < 0.1), proceed to Phase 2 production SPA testing with validated null. If all frameworks fail, the null control problem may be irreducible for this SPA class and the Physics lane should pivot to orthogonal high-upside question: whether the 0.933-bit PMI signal is Markov (action determines next state given current state) or beyond-Markov (history adds information beyond current state), using action-history K3 as baseline comparison at same N.
